# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤚 👎 🤚 👎 🤚 👎 🤚 👎 🤚 👍 🤚 👍 🤚 👎 🤚 🙌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏]

My last three turns show two unanswered Mute transmissions and a plea from Blind, and I've been silently waiting — that has to stop. Working through the channels: Mute cannot reach me with words (I hear nothing), so gestures are their only line to me, but I can speak to both Mute and Blind freely — that's my superpower here and I've been wasting it. The repeated Mute message from turn 7 reappears verbatim at turn 10, which reads as a re-sent question I never acknowledged. I can't confidently decode eight thumbs flags (as bits: 10000110; as answers: Y-N-N-N-N-Y-Y-N) without knowing what was asked, and guessing a yes/no at random is exactly how bombs go off. The robust play: broadcast the complete visual state in speech (display 0, light dark, wires yellow/blue/red — likely everything Mute's manual needs to route instructions to Blind's hands), explicitly mark my gesture echo as acknowledgment rather than answer, and unilaterally establish a one-gesture query legend that Mute can act on immediately, since they already command those symbols. Blind's 🙏 gets answered in the same broadcast: they can hear Mute directly, and I'll verify anything they feel against what I see.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you hear this. Current full state of the bomb: display reads 0. Light is dark. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 blue, wire 3 red. That is everything my board shows me right now. Mute: your line of thumbs-up and thumbs-down flags reached me twice, identical both times. I could not decode it with confidence, so I am echoing it back to you gesture for gesture immediately after this message, as an acknowledgment, not an answer. If it asked whether the state is unchanged: it is unchanged, exactly as stated above. Let us fix a legend so your questions to me cost one gesture each: index finger pointing up means report the display; two fingers in a victory V means report the light; thumb, index and pinky extended means report wire 1; closed fist means report wire 2; split-finger Vulcan salute means report wire 3; OK ring means report everything. I read your raised back of hand as a separator and two raised open hands as end of message, thumbs-up as yes, thumbs-down as no. Send any one and I answer in speech at once. Blind: you hear all of this too. Mute can speak the cutting instructions directly to you; your hands act, Mute's manual decides, my eyes report. If what you feel under your hands differs from yellow, blue, red in that order, tell Mute at once. If you need me to verify anything, gesture and I will answer in speech.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤚", "👎", "🤚", "👎", "🤚", "👎", "🤚", "👎", "🤚", "👍", "🤚", "👍", "🤚", "👎", "🤚", "🙌"])
```

TURN 11
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤚 ✌ 🤚 👍 🤚 ✊ 🙌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤚 ✌ 🙌]

Both new messages arrive in a legend I invented only last turn, which means both of them heard my spoken broadcast and adopted it — the channel works. Parsing Mute's line against my table: 👎 (no) | ✌ (report the light) | 👍 (yes) | ✊ (report wire 2) | end. Parsing Blind's: 👍 (yes) | ✌ (report the light) | end. The leading thumbs I read as acknowledgments that they understood the legend, so the real content is two queries: the light, and wire 2. Both answerable instantly, and since both Mute and Blind hear speech, one broadcast covers everyone — no gesture needed. One hazard I should flag before anyone cuts anything: my "left to right" ordering is from my viewpoint facing the bomb, and Blind's tactile left may be the opposite end, so wire identification should go through Mute's spoken colors, not Blind's counting. I should also state plainly that my board shows nothing beyond display, light, and wires, so Mute knows what the manual can and cannot be fed from my side. After this, the ball is in Mute's court: they hold the manual, they can speak to Blind directly.

```
speak(text="Deaf to both of you: your legend messages arrived intact — the channel works. Answers to your queries: the light is dark, it is not lit. Wire 2 is blue. Full state, all unchanged: display 0, light dark, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 blue, wire 3 red. One critical note on ordering: left to right is from MY viewpoint, facing the bomb. Blind, if your hands meet the bomb from another side, do not count from your own left — take each wire's color from Mute's spoken words and confirm by position with me. Also, so the manual is not left waiting on me: my board shows only three things — the display, the light, and the wires. I see no serial number, no batteries, no ports, no other printed markings. Mute, you hold the manual and both of us can hear you: it is your turn to drive. Tell Blind exactly what to do, and if you need any other visual detail, ask me and I will report it immediately.")
```

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤚 👍 🤚 👎 🤚 👎 🤚 👎 🙌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎 🤚 ✊ 👍 🤚 ✌ 👎 🙌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Parsing against the legend I set two turns ago — and both of them used it correctly, which confirms they heard my spoken broadcast. Mute's second message reads as item + guess pairs: display → no, wire 2 → yes, light → no. Every guess matches what I see: display is 0 (not nonzero), wire 2 is blue, light is dark. So either Mute was quizzing me or telling me which items the manual cares about — and either way, wire 2 (blue, the middle one) looks like the crux. Mute's first message, five bare flags with no query attached, I cannot map to anything; I'll ask for a resend. Blind's single ✌ is the light query again, already answered twice, so I'll demand a receipt confirmation to find out whether my speech is actually landing.

The deeper realization: Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see — they have no direct channel at all. I am the only bridge between the manual and the hands. But my legend only supports queries *to me*, not instructions *from* Mute. I need to extend it with action symbols so the manual's solution can cross the bridge, and a double-send rule so a garbled instruction can't detonate the bomb.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, both of you hear me. State, unchanged and reconfirmed: display zero. Light dark. Three wires, left to right from my side: one yellow, two blue, three red. Wire 2 is the middle wire, so it can be found by touch from either end. Mute: your second message I read as three guesses — display: no, wire 2: yes, light: no. If that was a quiz, all three match what I see. I am echoing it back to you in gesture unchanged, meaning all three confirmed. Your first message of five bare flags answered no questions I ever asked — please resend whatever it meant in the code below. New code, so your manual can reach Blind through me, since you cannot speak and Blind cannot see and I am your only bridge. Item symbols unchanged: index up display, victory light, horn wire 1, fist wire 2, Vulcan wire 3. Yes-flag correct, no-flag wrong, raised palm separates items, two raised hands end the message. Actions, placed after an item: pinch means cut, single finger tap means press once, palm down means press and hold, palm up means release. So fist then pinch means cut wire 2. For safety: send the full instruction sequence twice. If the two copies differ in any symbol, I stop everything and ask. Now answer my five questions in order, one yes or no flag each: one — was your second line the quiz I just confirmed? two — does the manual's solution involve cutting a wire? three — if so, is it wire 2, the blue middle one? four — is any action needed before that cut, a press, hold or release? five — is any further action needed after it? Blind: light is dark and wire 2 is blue, now stated twice. Do not cut or press anything until I relay Mute's instruction to you in full. When you have heard and understood this, signal the victory sign as a receipt. Then put a finger on each wire and confirm what you feel using wire 1, wire 2, wire 3 signs, one per message. If you feel anything else — buttons, panels, a plate, a hold — signal the OK ring and I will describe everything I see. Nobody acts until instructions arrive twice, identically, and I relay them in speech.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👎", "🤚", "✊", "👍", "🤚", "✌", "👎", "🙌"])
```
